To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phenomenon of envy is the common denominator among the three theories of elitism, group and power, and that envy is the key factor in the incapacity of the theories to account for the phenomenon of power in the absoluteness and absolutism of time and space.
the phenomenon of envy is a capacity gap in the elitism, group and power frameworks.

the three frameworks have a gap in the capacity to explain the phenomenon of envy; the phenomenon of envy is the common ingredient of those frameworks; and, the three frameworks have an incapacity to explain the phenomenon that power corrupts absolutely in the absolutism of time and space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: why is it that in the absoluteness in time and space, absolute power may never corrupt?

the following: (1) the phenomenon of envy as a framework of analysis, (2) the incapacity of the elitism, group and power frameworks to explain the phenomenon, (3) the ingredients of the phenomenon, and (4) the ingredients of those frameworks.
the following question: why do the theories of elitist, power, and group frameworks, which are based on envy, fail to understand envy?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phenomenon of envy has the capacity to bridge the gap in the three frameworks.

, in the absence of envy, the three frameworks would have been able to provide the answers to the questions they have been unable to answer, but, with envy, the three are not only unable to answer the questions, they are unable to even ask them.

envy is a phenomenon which has the capacity to be the framework of analysis for the three frameworks of elitism, groups, and power; and, that the phenomenon of envy is a framework that is more than capable of explaining why (absolute) absolute power may never corrupt in the absoluteness in time and space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

envy is a phenomenon that is not only capable of explaining the incapacity of the three frameworks to explain the phenomenon of absolute power, but also capable of explaining the phenomenon of absolute corruption.
the three frameworks have failed to explain the phenomenon of envy because they have not understood the nature of envy.
the phenomenon of envy is the common denominator of the three frameworks, and that the phenomenon of power is the common denominator among envy, group, and elitism.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the phenomenon of envy is the common thread that runs through the theories of elitist, group, and social power, which are the most important theories that have been developed by the social sciences to explain the phenomenon of power.
the phenomenon of envy is the key to understanding the incapacity of the three frameworks to account for why absolute power may never corrupt.
envy is the missing link in the three theories and that the social sciences need to develop a framework to study it.
